title: Private Upgrade Assistant — Compatibility Bridge & Canary Gate Integrator
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a user-facing 'Private Upgrade Assistant' feature for Redwood Private clusters that provides a compatibility bridge between versions, automated canary gate integration, and an orchestrated migration flow for VPC/on-prem customers. This ticket covers the control-plane orchestrator extension, schema-safe migration helpers, preflight compatibility checks, canary cohort configuration, and Console/CLI UX for initiating and monitoring upgrades. The work focuses on building a safe default path for minor and major version upgrades across LTS channels, while offering extensible hooks for custom migration steps used by customers with complex on-prem setups.
proposal: Deliver a companion service and CLI (rwu-upgradectl) that integrates with the existing Private control plane to run orchestrated upgrade campaigns. Key capabilities: 1) Compatibility Bridge: compute compatibility matrix for running components (agent <-> control plane, storage adapters, runtime kernels, and quantized model artifacts) and auto-select compatible variant fallbacks. 2) Canary Gate Integrator: let operators define cohorts and gate criteria (error rates, tail latency, token throughput, eval regression) for automated promotion/rollback. 3) Migration Modes: transactional online migrations (zero-downtime when possible), snapshot-and-roll-forward for heavy schema changes, and opt-in offline window flows. 4) Dry-run and plan export for customer approval. 5) Telemetry and runbook integration into Console with links to rollbacks & post-mortem templates.
design_notes: Architecture: add an Upgrade Assistant service next to the private control plane that orchestrates per-cluster cohorts. It uses the existing agent API for coordinated upgrade signaling and a new 'migration-run' CRD in the control plane state store. The Compatibility Bridge will derive compatibility from a version policy graph stored in the release registry: model ABI tags, runtime feature flags, and kernel-level compatibility labels. The Canary Gate Integrator consumes real-time metrics from the Console tracing/metrics API and enforces SLO-based promotion rules. Data migrations must be expressed as idempotent, reversible steps. DB migrations prefer online-safe transforms (backfill in background) and include a schema-shim to support dual-schema reads during transition. Signed artifacts: upgrade bundles are cryptographically signed and validated against tenant KMS/HSM when available. UX: Console shows a three-step flow (Preflight -> Canary -> Rollout) with editable gates, cohort sizing slider, and estimated risk score.
runbook_steps: Step 0: Run preflight (rwu-upgradectl preflight --cluster <id>) — runs compatibility checks and provides a generated plan.json
Step 1: Upload signed bundle to private registry or reference hosted release (release id)
Step 2: Create migration-run via control-plane API or Console; configure canary cohorts and gate thresholds
Step 3: Execute dry-run for selected cohort with traffic shadowing enabled (no live promotion)
Step 4: Run canary campaign: monitor SLOs for 2x expected latency window; automatic rollback on gate breach
Step 5: If canary passes, promote incrementally with staggered cohort windows and auto-scaling of dedicated pools when needed
Step 6: Run post-migration validations (smoke tests, eval prompts, embedding checks), then mark migration-run as complete
Step 7: If rollback required, run 'rwu-upgradectl rollback <run-id>' and execute snapshot restore or fallback variant routing depending on migration type
acceptance_criteria: Preflight produces a machine-readable plan.json and a human-friendly report with clear incompatibilities
Canary Gate Integrator can be configured via Console and CLI and enforces at least three distinct gate types (latency, error-rate, quality-regression)
A seeded internal test cluster can run a full orchestrated migration with zero client-visible downtime for control-plane upgrade path A->A+1
Data migrations for the reference test case complete without manual intervention and are idempotent when re-run
Signed-bundle verification works with tenant KMS and rejects tampered artifacts
Console shows a migration timeline, live gate metrics, and one-click rollback that triggers the documented rollback path
Basic run-level telemetry emitted to Console (start_time, stage, gate_status, rollback_reason, duration) and visible on the release dashboard
risks_mitigation: Risk: data-loss during schema migrations. Mitigation: require snapshot backup and schema-shim dual-read pattern; add a hard preflight blocker when incompatible transforms are detected
Risk: runaway canary due to incorrect gate thresholds. Mitigation: provide sane defaults derived from historical cluster baselines and require a minimum observation window before auto-promote
Risk: dependency on Console telemetry ingest. Mitigation: fallback to a local metrics evaluation engine inside Upgrade Assistant that can evaluate a subset of gates if Console is unreachable
Risk: customers with strict change windows. Mitigation: allow scheduled windows and manual approval hooks with signed acceptance in plan export
